Compose a foundation model inside a tidyverts model definition

Source: R/fable.R
TSFM.Rd

A fabletools::new_model_definition() wrapper so a pretrained checkpoint can be used inside fabletools::model() next to any other tidyverts model. The model is zero-shot: "training" binds the observed history for a key, and fabletools::forecast() runs the engine over it.

TSFM(
  formula,
  model_id,
  revision = NULL,
  quantile_levels = NULL,
  device = NULL,
  ...
)

Arguments

formula

A model formula naming the response, for example value.

model_id

Checkpoint id, as listed by zuk_models(). Use "stub" for the weight-free test fixture.

revision

NULL for the catalogue's immutable revision, or that exact revision string.

quantile_levels

Quantile levels to forecast; defaults to c(0.1, 0.5, 0.9).

device

Device requested for construction; see zuk_resolve_device().

...

Further load-affecting arguments passed to zuk_pretrained().

Value

A fabletools model definition.

Per key, not batched

fabletools evaluates one key at a time, so TSFM() runs the engine once per series. The checkpoint itself is loaded once and reused from the bounded resident cache (see zuk_pretrained() and zuk_cache_status()), but the forward passes are not batched across series. For a wide panel, prefer the batched route:

forecast(model, panel, h = 12) |> fabletools::as_fable()

What .mean holds

Every route carries the same predictive distribution, but they label the point forecast differently. fabletools derives .mean from the distribution, so a TSFM() fable reports the distribution's mean; forecast.zuk_model() and fabletools::as_fable() report the engine's exactly evaluated median. With few quantile levels the two diverge on a skewed forecast. median() of the distribution recovers the engine's point forecast on any route:

fc <- fabletools::forecast(fits, h = 12)
median(fc$value)   # the engine's point forecast

See also

forecast.zuk_model() for the batched panel route.

Examples

history <- tsibble::tsibble(time = 1:12, value = cumsum(1:12), index = time)
fits <- fabletools::model(history, zukzeit = TSFM(value, model_id = "stub"))
fabletools::forecast(fits, h = 3)
#> # A fable: 3 x 4 [1]
#> # Key:     .model [1]
#>   .model   time       value .mean
#>   <chr>   <dbl>      <dist> <dbl>
#> 1 zukzeit    13 quantile[3]    78
#> 2 zukzeit    14 quantile[3]    78
#> 3 zukzeit    15 quantile[3]    78
zuk_unload("stub")
